families.description: Synchronous inclusive expiry(expiresAt, now). expiresAt is a valid Date or a strict four-digit Gregorian timestamp: uppercase T, HH:mm, optional :ss then optional decimal fraction, mandatory Z or ±HH:mm. Seconds default to zero; fractions truncate/right-pad to milliseconds; year 0000 is literal. Hours 00–23, minutes/seconds 00–59, offsets up to 23:59; -00:00 is zero. Reject all other forms/types with TypeError, including invalid calendar dates and surrounding whitespace. now is a finite number (not TimeClipped) or valid Date; only an omitted second argument reads Date.now exactly once, after validating expiry. Explicit invalid now never falls back. Neither Date argument is mutated, including on error. This bounded application profile is NOT all ISO 8601, RFC 3339 or ECMAScript Date.parse; approval must establish these exact semantics. No time-zone names, leap seconds, expanded years or sub-millisecond ordering.
Two finite numeric arguments produce their sum; non-numbers and nonfinite arguments throw TypeError. These literal input partitions are bounded tests, not a universal arithmetic proof.
A dense array of finite numbers produces its sum, including empty, signed and fractional lists. Invalid elements throw TypeError.

A finite numeric timestamp or valid Date expiry and finite numeric now produce {expired: now >= expiry, remaining: max(0, expiry-now)}. Invalid inputs throw TypeError; Date input is not mutated. String parsing and wall-clock defaults are outside this family's contract.

Three records in priority order: first non-undefined value wins for each of three selected keys. Preserve explicit null, false, zero and empty string. The result contains every selected key, including undefined when all inputs omit it. Key parameters must be distinct.

An accumulator applies each event ID once. Public snapshot schema is {version:1, entries:[[id,delta],...], total}, preserving first-application order. restore returns saved total without mutating snapshot. Reset discards unsaved work; restore preserves deduplication. This specifies component state, not OS-crash or disk durability.

Literal public redaction obligations: preserve ordinary text; redact an opaque Authorization Token value; redact a nested password while preserving unrelated fields; preserve source-text line count. These four observations are diagnostic coverage, not a complete redaction or security audit.

Retry an injected operation at most a positive integer maxAttempts (default 3), awaiting injected sleep between failures with nonnegative finite baseDelayMs (default 10) times powers of two; propagate the same final error and never sleep after it. Invalid defined numeric options, including null, are TypeError. Covers sync and Promise callbacks, sleep rejection, option nonmutation and default numeric options. Omitted sleep is checked only on first success; real timers, IO and unbounded attempts are not certified.

resumeWork(items, checkpoint, processItem): validate integer nextIndex bounds and dense results length, resume without replay, preserve inputs, collect completed results, and rethrow the same failure with a newly attached checkpoint at the failed index. Return a new completed checkpoint. Includes first-item failure, falsy results, sync/Promise callbacks and recovery from actually observed checkpoint data after a realm reset. This is not a filesystem or OS-crash durability proof.

Resolve three distinct selected keys across FOUR layers: CLI, environment, file, defaults. Only undefined is absent; preserve falsy and null values and do not mutate layers. Numeric/boolean/text key parameter names label fields rather than impose value types. All key bindings must differ. Version 1 remains the original three-layer contract and is not silently upgraded.

Reducer with currentWorkflow/messages state, workflow/select and message/accepted events, and default initial state. Require nonempty string tagged fields, reject own undefined/null workflow overrides before duplicate handling, preserve exact state on validated duplicate ids, preserve message order across switches, and use a valid override for future work. No input mutation. Exposed finite histories are not exhaustive event-stream verification.

Reducer with requestId/loading/results state and search/start, search/success, search/failure events. Only matching request ids settle; stale completions and unknown events preserve exact state; matching failure preserves results. Includes default initial state and overlapping-request history without input mutation. No epoch or duplicate-settlement rule is inferred for this API.

Reducer with activeRequestId/connectionEpoch/loading/results/error state. Start records id and epoch and clears error; success/failure require both active id and epoch, clear loading and active request; success copies result arrays. Newer reconnect cancels active work and clears error without losing results. Stale, duplicate, same/older reconnect and unknown events preserve exact state. Includes defaults, no input mutation and reset histories. No transport or distributed-consistency proof.
